statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-53859 is a buffer over-read in nginx's ngx_mail_smtp_module: a crafted login or password used with the "none" authentication method can make a worker process disclose memory to the authentication server. nginx.org lists 0.7.22 to 1.29.0 as vulnerable and 1.29.1 and later as fixed (https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html, https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000152786), and the 1.28.1 stable release carries the same fix (https://nginx.org/en/CHANGES-1.28, https://nginx.org/download/patch.2025.smtp.txt, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/765642b86e0df1b5ef37f42522be7d08d95909c9). For Alpine 3.23, the DHI nginx build 1.28.0-r8 ships nginx 1.28.0 built from Alpine's 1.28.0-r8 recipe, which carries no backport of this fix (Alpine lists it as fixed in 1.28.2-r0, https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/nginx/APKBUILD). The 1.28.1-r0 build, published for aarch64, ships nginx 1.28.1, and every later build (1.28.2-r0 to 1.28.3-r9 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r7) ships a fixed release, as each nginx binary's version banner shows on x86_64 and aarch64. So the range ends at 1.28.1-r0.

The 1.28.1-r0 build, published for aarch64, ships nginx 1.28.1, and every later build (1.28.2-r0 to 1.28.3-r9 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r7) ships a fixed release, as each nginx binary's version banner shows on x86_64 and aarch64. So the range ends at 1.28.1-r0.
